articleTitle: Calculation of Jiles-Atherton hysteresis model's parameters using mix of chaos optimization algorithm and simulated annealing algorithm
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A mix of chaos optimization method and simulated annealing method to calculate the Jiles-Atherton (JA) model's parameters is proposed in this paper. The new method costs less time in calculating the JA model's parameters. During the search performance, the local extreme value can be avoided effectively. A modified JA model is applied in this paper, choose the magnetic flux as the confident variable. The model can be directly used in time-domain finite-element calculations applied to the magnetic vector potential formulation. The curve which calculated using the obtained parameters is well agreed to the measured curve by experiment.

articleTitle: Application of the linear and nonlinear inversion algorithms on two-dimensional experimental electromagnetic data
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper describes the linear and nonlinear inversion algorithms for reconstructing two inhomogeneous dielectric targets in an anechoic chamber in a controlled environment. The applied algorithms are the linear multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm combined with the time reversal (TR) imaging and two nonlinear iterative algorithms—two domain integral equation based methods, namely the contrast source inversion (CSI) algorithm and the multiplicative regularized contrast source inversion (MR-CSI) algorithm. The inversion results, which are presented and compared for the transverse magnetic (TM) and transverse electric (TE) polarization datasets using the multi-frequency multi-bistatic measurements, verify the capability, the accuracy and the efficiency of the MR-CSI algorithm.

articleTitle: Gradient index microwave lens using metal strip
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Metal strips settled in a particular array provide the unique electromagnetic properties. In this paper, the electromagnetic parameters of the metal strip array with different geometric size are given and analysed by effective medium theory, which is the theoretical basis of gradient index microwave lens demonstrating the field deflection and focusing effect. In order to display the properties, we designed a 4 X 10 metal strip array and obtained its field distribution by simulation. The result agreed well with the theoretical prediction.

articleTitle: Parallel high-order FE-BI-MLFMA for scattering by large and deep coated cavities
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A fast high-order finite element-boundary integral-multilevel fast multipole algorithm (FE-BI-MLFMA) recently has been presented for scattering by large and deep cavities. The bottleneck of this algorithm is pointed out in this paper. A parallelization approach of this FE-BI-MLFMA is presented and implemented to eliminate this bottleneck. Numerical experiments demonstrate the parallel efficiency of this parallelization approach. The capability of this parallel FE-BI-MLFMA is demonstrated by computing scattering by a big and deep brick cavity with 15λ×15λ×100λ. Numerical examples of cavities loaded with obstacles, including a circular cavity loaded by an array of straight blades model are performed to verify the high efficiency and accuracy of the parallel FE-BI-MLFMA.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized Fabry-Perot Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The circularly polarized Fabry-Perot resonator (FPR) antenna is presented, which consists of a primary radiator backed with a metal ground plate and a partially reflective surface covered plate composed of appropriate frequency selective surface (FSS) structure with ring elements. For the proposed antenna, an L-probe is utilized to feed the patch orthogonally, a Wilkinson power combiner is connected to the feeds to generate circular polarization, which is act as primary radiator of the antenna. The antenna possessed a 10-dB return loss bandwidth of 15.5%, and has a 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 13.2%. A bandwidth of 14.2% for -3 dB directivity drop from peak value is also obtained.

articleTitle: Unsplit-field formulations for the higher-order PML
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Based on the stretched coordinate perfectly matched layer (SC-PML) formulations and the auxiliary differential equation (ADE) method, an unsplit-field implementation of the higher-order PML scheme with more than one pole is proposed for truncating the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) lattices. The higher-order PML has the advantages of both the conventional PML and the complex frequency shifted PML (CFS-PML). A numerical validation of the proposed formulations is given through a 2D TE-polarized electromagnetic wave interaction with an infinitely long perfectly electric conductor (PEC) sheet with the finite width. It is shown in the numerical simulation that the proposed PML formulations with the higher-order scheme are efficient in terms of attenuating both the low-frequency propagating waves and evanescent waves and reducing late-time reflections, and also hold much better absorbing performances than the conventional SC-PML and the convolutional PML (CPML) with the CFS scheme.

articleTitle: Integrated log-periodic antenna for Terahertz applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Planar antenna has special advantages in terahertz applications; it can easy integrate other devices such diodes and SIS. Logperiodic antenna is a type of classical wide-band antenna. But planar antenna has characteristics of low gain and wide beam, and these often become disadvantages. To integrate a horn and back cavity with planar antenna is a good way overcome these disadvantages. MEMS (Micro-electromechanical Systems) technology has its benefits to manufacture very small size devices, and the accuracy can be achieved micron level. In this paper, a novel integrated log-periodic antenna at 0.9 THz totally based on MEMS technology was proposed. This kind antenna maintains the advantage of wide bandwidth of log-periodic and also has good radiation performance. The processing of this type horn antenna combine two kind MEMS techniques, silicon dry etching and silicon dry etch,. The main superiority of this kind integrated antenna is that it has more tunable parameters than other type MEMS-based antennas. From the results of analysis, we can see that integrated antennas meet demands of different applications can be well designed by optimizing these parameters.

articleTitle: A bandpass filter using LTCC System-on-Package (SOP) Technology
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: LTCC System-on-Package (SOP) Technology is presently the most effective method for realizing the miniaturization of wireless front-end applications. In this paper, the development of highly integrated three-dimensional (3-D) filter solutions in multilayer low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technologies is presented for compact, low-cost wireless frontend modules utilizing system-on-package (SOP) technology. An asymmetrical dumbbell-shaped capacitor and wideband circuit design method was used to improve the filter characteristic. The embedded filter demonstrate an excellent performance (1L <; 1 dB, 3 dB BW 5 ≥ 27% at the centre frequency of 1.3 GHz) and great potential for high level of 3-D integration in wireless system. The BPF circuit is based on the quasi-lumped filter topology and some broadband technology was adopted. It has been simulated and optimized by Ansoft HFSS. The measured results agree very well with the full-wave electromagnetic designed responses.

articleTitle: Research on the influence scope of periodic slots on leaky coaxial cables
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Calculation of the radiation field is an important work in the novel leaky coaxial cable (LCX) design. By analyzing the influence scope of the slots on the LCX, the minimum length that should be employed in the calculation of LCX can be determined. In this paper, a method of finding the influence scope of slots on LCX is proposed. In this method, the influence scope of slot is studied by analyzing the change of near field distribution when the cable length increases. After the influence scope is gotten, the minimum length of the cable is also obtained. In addition, the radiation field distribution of a single period is also given, which can also be used to determine the influence scope of slots.

articleTitle: A broadband circular polarization patch antenna with differential-feeding
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A broadband circular polarization patch antenna, differential-fed by a pair of folded plate, is proposed. The use of the two patches can broaden the bandwidth and the differential-feeding can provide a good symmetrical pattern. The impedance bandwidth (VSWR<;2) of the proposed antenna is 38.5%. The axis ratio (AR) at the centre frequency of 2 GHz is 2.3 dB in measurement. Besides, the radiation pattern, both E-plane and H-plane, are symmetrical respectively.

articleTitle: The realization of high isolation and wide band 4×4 microstrip Butler matrix
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A high isolation and wideband 4 × 4 Butler matrix is designed and fabricated on a single-layer PCB substrate in this paper, which covers the frequency band from 1.92 to 2.17 GHz. The measured S-parameters show that its return loss and isolation are better than -23 dB and -26 dB, respectively, with its good performance achieved for real application.

articleTitle: A 3D design software for Quasi-optical systems based on integrated methods
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Diffracted Gaussian beam analysis (DGBA) is a fast method for Quasi-optical systems analysis, and Periodic Method of Moment (PMM) is an efficient method for analyzing Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS). This paper introduces a 3D design software for Quasi-optical systems namely SiMatrix based on the integration of the DGBA and PMM. The SiMatrix offers the functionalities of visualized 3D modeling, systematic simulation and built-in post-processing. Those functionalities greatly facilitate the design and analysis of a Quasi-optical system.

articleTitle: ISAR imaging of multiple targets based on FrFT-CLEAN
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging of multiple warhead targets in the same antenna beam is a big challenge when they are overlapping in the same range bin. Existing methods are usually based on single target motion compensation and they can't get clear ISAR image of multiple targets. This paper presents a new algorithm for ISAR imaging of multiple targets based on Fractional Fourier Transform (FrFT) CLEAN method to separate signals of different targets. Firstly, signal model of multiple targets is given. Then analyzed each target has different Doppler history, the signals of a certain target in a range bin correspond to a batch of multicomponent liner frequency modulation (LFM) signals. Theoretical analysis and computer simulations show the proposed method can generate the images from multiple target echoes effectively.

articleTitle: A rectangular waveguide-microstrip transition based on the principle of magnetic coupling for millimeter-wave
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A novel rectangular waveguide-microstrip transition for millimeter-wave frequency band is presented in this paper. The transition circuit is based on the principle of magnetic-field excitation. The triangular ring circuit, which is placed on the dielectric substrate inserted to the E-face of the waveguide, is used to achieve the mode conversion of the main mode between the rectangular waveguide and microstrip line. The structure has the advantages of low insertion loss, wide frequency range, small size and non-debug. The measured results show that the insertion loss of the back-to-back transition is less than 2.5 dB in the whole Ka-band.

articleTitle: Design of circular polarization microstrip antenna in RFID reader for 5.8GHz Electronic Toll Collection application
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, the design indices of the antenna used in electronic toll collection submitted to the national specifications of China have been drawn out and then a right-hand circular polarization microstrip array antenna subject to the specification is presented. The simulation result obtained by ADS software show that the performances of the presented antenna meet the needs of system very well.

articleTitle: Research of the ambiguity restraint in five-element cross-shaped array
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The ambiguity problem of direction of arrival (DOA) estimation in uniform cross-shaped array is caused by the large element-spacing. From the viewpoint of matrix, the ambiguity can be described as the complete equality of the steering-vectors generated by the estimated false angle and true angle. In order to break the balance, which the steering-vectors generated by the false and true angle are completely equal, a novel method is proposed, in which an additional element with small spacing to the origin is added in the five-element uniform cross-shaped array. From the results of mathematical analysis and simulation, it is found that the method proposed can revise the steering-vector, restrain the false peak and improve the accuracy of DOA estimation greatly.

articleTitle: Applications of Carbon nanotube technology for next-generation high speed and microwave circuits
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have demonstrated promising electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties. For example, CNTs have long mean free paths in the order of several micrometers (as compared to 40 nm for Cu at room temperature), resulting in low resistivity and possible ballistic transport, and an isolated CNT can carry current densities in excess of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> even at an elevated temperature of 250°C. These unique properties make them exciting prospects for a variety of applications in microelectronics/nanoelectronics, spintronics, optics, as well as material science, mechanical and biological fields, and even fundamental areas like relativistic quantum mechanics and condensed matter physics. This paper reviews the current state of research (including some research achievements of the author's group) in applications of carbon nanotube technology for high speed and microwave circuits. At first both electrical and thermal modeling and broadband characterization for various CNTs (single walled CNTs, multi walled CNTs and CNT bundles) are presented and compared each other and with conventional conductor materials to give guidelines for their prospective applications. Then various applications, including for high speed interconnects and vias, microwave passives such as inductors, capacitors, resonators, antennas, and some other fields, are introduced and discussed. The results from simulation or experiment show that some performance, such as the delay of interconnect and quality factor of microwave inductor, of interconnects or microwave passives based on CNTs is much better than that based on traditional conductors, indicating that the emerging nano-scale materials have great potential in applications for next-generation high speed and microwave circuits.

articleTitle: Extending the three-dimensional LOD-FDTD method to lumped load and voltage source with impedance
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, the three-dimensional locally one-dimensional finite difference time domain (LOD-FDTD) method is extended to include lumped elements calculation. The algorithm of the three-dimensional (3-D) LOD-FDTD which includes lumped elements calculation is derived, and then, a complex metal cavity feed by a voltage source with lumped resistance and loaded by a lumped load is simulated. The numerical result is presented to show the validity of the algorithm. The proposed LOD-FDTD method is found to use less CPU time comparing with traditional finite difference time domain (FDTD) method.

articleTitle: IE-FFT solution of volume-surface integral equation for composite conducting-dielectric objects
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The paper extends the integral equation fast Fourier transform (IE-FFT) to the solution of volume-surface integral equation (VSIE). The volume integral equation is formulated for dielectric object and the electric field integral equation is formulated for conducting surfaces. The floating stencil topology is implemented to further reduce the memory requirement and CPU time for the IE-FFT solution. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: An efficient parallel SAI preconditioner for multilevel fast multipole algorithm for scattering by extremely large complex targets
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A highly efficient parallel SAI preconditioner is presented. This preconditioner is incorporated into our previously well developed parallel MLFMA code, and successfully computes scattering by a sphere with a diameter of 750 wavelengths, involving over 315 millions unknowns. The capability of this parallel SAI preconditioner is further demonstrated on computing scattering by an extremely large tank with a size of over 300-wavelengths containing around 35 millions unknowns, where convergence cannot be achieved without this SAI preconditioner.

articleTitle: An improved method of extracting permeability using SVM
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The method extracting permeability from scattering coefficients was studied in this paper. The support vector machine (SVM) method is used to solve the inverse problem of parameters extraction. The mapping relationship is set up by calculating a large number of S parameters from the samples with different permeability by using transmission line theory. The simulated data set is used as training data set for SVM. After the training, the SVM is used to predict the permeability of material from the scattering coefficients.

articleTitle: An iterative scheme for Gaussian beam expansion of electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Point matching technique is applied to a pyramidal horn antenna to expand its aperture field in a wide angular range in terms of Gaussian beams using the Jacobi iterative method. The obtained far field pattern is compared with the results of Gabor's Gaussian beam expansion. Convergence, speed, the impact of initial condition and the selection of sample points is discussed. The implemented point matching scheme is almost as fast and accurate as the Gabor's expansion. It can even be faster and more accurate in some cases especially when the Gaussian beams are neither wide-waisted nor narrow-waisted.

articleTitle: Novel microstrip antenna for 2.4 GHz with harmonic Rejection
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Novel arc-slot microstrip antenna with harmonic rejection property is presented. By optimize antenna parameters ,second and third harmonic rejection better than 15 dB have been achieved .Also patch size is compact and we have achieve size reduction about 40% of conventional square patch antenna with probe-fed.

articleTitle: Matching network design for a double band PIFA antenna via simplified real frequency technique
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper uses simplified real frequency technique in designing the dual-frequency antenna matching network, and takes PIFA(900/1800MHz) as example. It could expand the antenna bandwidth and reduce the return loss. By using ADS software, we can turn the lumped network into the distributed network. The results show that the frequency band increases from 11MHz to 14MHz, from 205MHz to 257MHz, increasing about 27.3%and 25.4%separately.

articleTitle: Miniature dual-mode bandpass filter using hexagonal meander loop resonator
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A new dual-mode microstrip bandpass filter using hexagonal meander loop resonator with a circular patch is presented in this paper. Only one mode characteristics are affected by changing the size of the circular patch. A coupling matrix is synthesized and validates the proposed coupling scheme. Compact size, low insertion loss and high selectivity characteristics are realized by this type of filter. The filter is evaluated by experiment and simulation with good agreement.

articleTitle: Design of tri-reflector Compact Antenna Test Range
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Compact antenna test range (CATR) is an effective way for millimeter/sub millimeter antenna testing. In this paper, geometric optics (GO) method is utilized to design a tri-reflector CATR, the advantages of which lie in high reflector usage and low manufacture cost compared with conventional single reflector CATR. Kinematic and dynamic ray tracing theory is used to determine surface parameters of the two shaped subreflectors during the process. A double-Gregorian tri-reflector CATR is designed as an example at last.

articleTitle: Terahertz applications and technology
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Research has been carried out in the THz region for several decades. Until fairly recently, the main drive came from applications such as radio astronomy, later followed by planetary, cometary and atmospheric science. Arguably, without these driving influences it is unlikely that many of the recent technological breakthroughs would have occurred. This paper presents an overview of space and terrestrial related applications and technologies. The more traditional and some most likely future applications will be treated.

articleTitle: Printed triple-t monopole antenna for 2.4, 5.2, and 5.8 GHz WLAN operations
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A novel three-band printed monopole antenna is proposed, which is composed of three stacked T-shaped monopoles with different sizes, and is analyzed by using the Finite Difference Time Domain Method (FDTD). The proposed antenna was fabricated and tested. The simulated and experimental results of impedance bandwidths of the antenna can meet the demand of WLAN operations in the 2.4, 5.2, and 5.8 GHz bands. The antenna has a simple profile, and can easily be fed by 50 Ω microstrip line. Moreover, simulated and experimental results with different parameters of the antenna are given.

articleTitle: An LTCC duplexer for GSM/DCS applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A miniaturized quasi-lumped element multiplayer duplexer is designed and fabricated using a standard low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technique for application of GSM/DCS communication system. Several transmission zeros are specially introduced to provide sharp slope sides and enhance the isolation between the lowpass and highpass channels. An additional transmission zero is located in the stopband of lowpass filter to improve the high frequency rejection. The expected superior performance is validated by the measured S-parameters, which are in good agreement with the simulated results. The duplexer has the advantages of compactness, high integration, and low cost.

articleTitle: Study on terahertz time domain spectroscopy of pine wood nematode disease
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Pulsed terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) is a coherent technique, in which both the amplitude and the phase of a THz pulse are measured. Coherent detection enables direct calculations of both the imaginary and the real parts of the refractive index without using the Kramers-Kronig relations. In this paper, the spectroscopic characteristics of pine wood nematode and diseased pine wood in the THz regime are studied. In order to look for a rapid spectroscopic discrimination method for the disease, we measure the transmission characteristics of a Bursaphelenchus xylophilus (Bx) sample and a Bursaphelenchus mucronatus (Bm) sample by terahertz time domain spectroscopy. The measured time domain spectrums and corresponding frequency domain spectrums are compared to distinguish them from their absorption characteristics. At the same time, we also measure the transmission characteristics of a healthy Pinus massoniana (Pm) wood sample, a Pm with Bm wood sample, and a diseased Pm wood sample by THz-TDS and compare their difference in THz absorption spectrum and diffraction dispersive spectrum to confirm the effect of Bx on Pm by the absorption coefficient and refractive index.

articleTitle: Small smart antenna composed of reconfigurable Inverted F-type Antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, a small size electronically steerable parasitic array radiator (ESPAR) antenna composed of six inverted F-type antennas (IFAs) that covers the frequency band from 2.4 to 2.5 GHz is proposed. Each of the IFAs can be reconfigured either as a driven element or a parasitic element equally. The radius of the proposed ESPAR antenna is 11.5 mm, which enables handheld wireless devices such as mobile phone and walkie talkie to employ a smart antenna. Despite its small size, the proposed ESPAR antenna achieves a gain of 3.5 dBi and a front-back ratio of 7 dB. The beam forming can be achieved by tuning the reactive load of varactors on each IFA radiator.

articleTitle: A modified FDTD implementation for EM scattering by stratified medium for oblique incidence by TM wave
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A modified FDTD implementation, by which EM wave transmission characteristic can be analyzed for oblique incidence on stratified medium, is proposed. This method transforms two-dimensional electromagnetic wave transmission question as one-dimensional question, FDTD iterative formula are deduced in the TM wave oblique incidence situation, and the connection boundary (CB) and the absorbing boundary condition (ABC) in the oblique incidence situation are carried out the revision. The EM wave reflection coefficients of the medium slab and isotropic plasma slab are calculated in the TM wave oblique incidence situation, the computed results and the analytic solutions are in good agreement. The computed results indicate the accuracy and validity of this method.

articleTitle: Simulation design of submillimeter wave subharmonic mixer
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper introduces the circuit simulation design of a submillimeter wave subharmonic mixer. Detailed simulation design procedures of mixer diodes, transition, filter and matching circuits are depicted. The mixer using commercially available DBES105a GaAs Schottky barrier diodes is designed to operate in an RF frequency of 361 GHz when supplied with a LO frequency of 180 GHz. The result of simulation shows that the conversion loss of the mixer is less than 15 dB in an RF frequency from 357.5 GHz to 362.5 GHz with a LO power of 6 dBm.

articleTitle: Effects of higher order analytical evaluation of integrals on the accuracy of the on-surface discretized boundary equation method for two-dimensional scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The on-surface discretized boundary equation (OS-DBE) method for two-dimensional scattering problems achieves high accuracy for the current solution, primarily due to the features of the method itself, but also due to higher order analytical evaluation of the integrals concerned. In this paper, we provide detailed formulation of higher order analytical integral evaluation and show its effects on the solution accuracy. In view of the fast multiple method (FMM) applied to the solution of the OS-DBE matrices, the higher order approximations to far interactions are also derived. The method of moments without or with FMM implementation is incidentally addressed regarding this subject. Abnormal phenomena associated with higher order evaluation that may appear in the magnetic field expressions or magnetic field integral equations are discussed.

articleTitle: Suppressing cosite interference of shipboard antennas using AIC technology
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Based on the characteristics of cosite coupling interference between transmitting and receiving antennas in a same battleship, this paper analyses the principle of interference suppression using adaptive interference cancellation (AIC) method, and describes an implementing scheme. At last, an experiment programme and some results are provided to demonstrate the effectiveness of the AIC system. Experiment results prove that an interference cancellation rate (ICR) about 40 dB can be achieved using this method.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic metamaterials: Recent advances on the theory, experiments, and applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Electromagnetic metamaterials, first known as left-handed materials (LHM) or negative refractive index materials (NIM), have attracted intensive attention in the electromagnetic communities in the past years. Right now, the concept of metamaterials has much broader scope than that of LHM or NIM. Metamaterials are actually macroscopic composites of periodic or non-periodic structures, whose function is due to both the cellular architectures and the chemical compositions. This paper presents some recent progress on metamaterials, including the optical transformation theory, experiments on metamaterials, new physical discoveries and phenomena, the relationship between the computational electromagnetics and metamaterials, and real applications on microwave components and antennas.

articleTitle: Research on the impact of amplitude and phase imbalance on the angle measurement and calibration method in digital monopulse radar system
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A base band sum-difference scenario used in digital monopulse radar system is introduced in this paper. The angle measurement error caused by the amplitude and phase imbalance of the receiving channels is also analyzed based on this system structure. A digital calibration method as well as the compensation result is represented.

articleTitle: Planar waveguide antennas for Millimeter-wave systems
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Planar waveguide arrays are promising candidates for high gain, high efficiency antennas in millimeter-wave systems. Authors are driving forward a 5 year project on "RF coexisting technology on high speed baseband IC for millimeter wave radio systems" which is supported by Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) funding as well as Industry' s participation. This paper introduces the project and the planar waveguide antennas which characterize it. Among various activities in the project, bandwidth enhancement of the series fed hollow waveguide arrays as well as the loss estimation of the post-wall waveguide antennas are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: PO-MOM analysis of an antenna with reflector enclosed in an electrically large radome
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The hybrid method combining physical optics (PO) and method of moments (MOM) is proved to be an excellent method for an electrically large radiation system. In this paper, a simple and efficient method for dealing with the shading problem is presented to analyze an antenna-radome system with a PEC reflector, which also roots in the basic PO and IPO theory used in shading analysis for the scattering problem. Furthermore, the division principle of PO and MOM regions is discussed carefully for less computer cost.

articleTitle: Design of cylindrical conformal microstrip GPS antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, the GPS (global position system) antenna array which is conformal with missile is present. The basic theory and design method of cylindrical conformal antenna are described. Numerical and measured results of the antenna array radiation characteristic show this antenna array can radiate an omnidirectional normal to the axis of the pattern. So it has great practicability.

Author Keywords: omnidirectional pattern Cylindrical Conformal antenna array

articleTitle: Joint time-frequency micro-Doppler analysis of electromagnetic backscattering from micro-motion object
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Mechanical vibration or rotation of structures in a target may induce frequency modulation on returned signals and generate side-bands about the center frequency of the target's body Doppler frequency. The modulation due to vibrations, which is usually at very low frequencies relative to the body Doppler frequency, is called micro-Doppler phenomenon. Radar cross section (RCS) of an object is a function of aspect angle and frequency. When the object is rotating or has a rotating structure on it, the electromagnetic (EM) backscattering is subjects to modulations simultaneously in amplitude and phase that result in asymmetric Doppler spectra about the carrier frequency. The characteristics of the spectra are determined by the geometry, dimension, and the rotation rate of the rotating part.

articleTitle: Fast RCS computation in both spatial and frequency domains using adaptive MBPE technique
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Sampling is one of the key techniques of the model based parameter estimation (MBPE). The ill-conditioning of the data matrix caused by the high polynomial order of the fitting-model occurs frequently. How to divide the oversized fitting-model into smaller ones is discussed and an adaptive sampling scheme is proposed in this paper. Since the equispaced approach is firstly applied and there is no need to add additional checking points, the searching time is greatly reduced. Numerical results have proved the validity and the efficiency of the method.

articleTitle: A novel 3–5 GHz low noise amplifier using an active inductor
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper presents a novel 3-5 GHz SiGe HBT low noise amplifier (LNA) using an active inductor. The use of active inductor instead of passive inductor can greatly reduce the chip area. The active inductor compensates the decrease of gain of the amplifier and improves the gain flatness in the high-frequency band. The simulation results show the LNA has gain (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub>) of 24.856 dB with 0.056 dB variation over the 3 GHz to 5 GHz band. The matched input and output reflectance (S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> and S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">22</sub>) are less than -18 dB and -14 dB, respectively. In addition, LNA is unconditionally stable over the entire band.

articleTitle: Design of EMC testing equipment for mobile phones
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: We have designed a testing equipment to detect the mobile phone electromagnetic interference. We also have compared the sensitivity of our testing equipment with other two testing systems. Measurement results demonstrate that our mobile phone EMC testing equipment has a high sensitivity up to -125 dBm in the natural environment.

articleTitle: Analysis of the conically conformal microstrip antennas by CFDTD method and its parallelization
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, the detailed characteristics of the conically conformal microstrip antenna element and the mutual coupling effects between two antenna elements are analyzed by using the rigorous conformal FDTD algorithm in the Cartesian coordinate. The effectiveness and correctness of the method are verified by comparing the numerical results with the corresponding ones presented in the existing literatures and the experimental results. Based on the parallel FDTD method, the characteristics of microstrip antenna array mounted on the conical ground is also investigated.

articleTitle: RFID Application in IT Assets Management
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: With the demand of IT services applied for the enterprises increasing, a more efficient and secure IT assets management system is now needed for every company. This paper discusses the RFID application in the IT assets management with details, which involves system structure, hardware configuration and information process. Moreover, the author provides with several practicable approaches to configure cabinet RFID antennas, which can be used under different situations. At last, the paper draws the conclusion that a RFID assets management can save time and resources, while improving information accuracy as well. It is proved through data and simulations to be a necessary means when managing IT infrastructure within the company.

articleTitle: Integrated waveguide slot antenna for V-band based on LTCC technology
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A design of LTCC multi-layer slot antenna is introduced, which is based on classical design theory of slot antenna and LTCC technology. According to full-wave electromagnetic(EM) simulation, the antenna, intended for use in high integrated 60 GHz radios, has achieved an acceptable impedance bandwidth from 53 GHz to 70 GHz and a peak gain of 5.2 dB at 68.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Predicting far-field RCS from near-field data based on MOM
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A technique to predict far-field RCS from near-field data is described. The method utilizes near-field data to determine equivalent sources over a fictitious surface which encompasses the target made by perfect electric conductor (PEC) and these sources are used to ascertain the far-field RCS. An electric field integral equation (EFIE) is developed to relate the near-field to the equivalent sources. RWG basis function is involved and makes the EFIE simple. The equivalent sources can be expanded by RWG basis function according to method of moments (MOM) procedure. The integral equation can be transformed into a matrix with the equivalent sources decoupling from the equation. The matrix equation is solved with the least squares techniques. Numerical simulation of this technique is presented. The results of the equivalent sources show high accuracy compared to the scattering RCS calculated by the software FEKO.

articleTitle: Design of a W-band Subharmonically pumped mixer based on a hybrid Schottky diode model
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper presents a hybrid Schottky diode model for mixer design. The model consists of two parts: the passive part and the active part. The passive part is built according to the dimensions of the diode which can be analyzed by EM simulator and the active part is built according to the I-V characteristic which can be analyzed by harmonic balanced simulator. Based on the proposed model, a W-band Subharmonically pumped mixer was designed, whose conversion loss is below 14 dB from 85 GHz to 93 GHz.

articleTitle: An accelerate method for the simulation of High-Power Microwave propagation through the atmosphere
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In the simulation of High-Power Microwave (HPM) propagation in the atmosphere, the distribution of HPM at the target point is only need to be concerned, but its distribution of each points in space do not need to know, one can consider separate the propagation space first, add an absorbing boundary at the sub-point, save the HPM data at this point, and as a source for the follow-up calculation add to the subsequent step, completion of data transfer. By this cycle of processing will play a role of to save computing time and computing memory, so as to achieve the effect of accelerated.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering by cylindrical arrays of circular rods
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A semi-analytical and rigorous method for analyzing two-dimensional scattering of electromagnetic waves by a cylindrical array is presented. The cylindrical array is formed by parallel circular rods of infinite length which are symmetrically distributed on a circular cylindrical surface. The proposed method uses the T-matrix of a circular rod in isolation and the reflection and transmission matrices of the scattered fields expressed in terms of the cylindrical harmonic waves as the basis. The details to obtain the reflection and transmission matrices in closed form are discussed. The results are extended to the generalized reflection and transmission matrices which can be applied to the analysis of electromagnetic scattering by multilayered cylindrical arrays of circular rods.

articleTitle: Study of an ultra wideband planar elliptical dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra wideband planar elliptical dipole antenna for EMC measurements. Two elliptical elements of the dipole antenna are printed on a circular dielectric substrate and fed by a coaxial cable. The performance and characteristics of the proposed antenna are investigated in order to understand the operation of the antenna.

articleTitle: Parabolic wave equation for radio propagation over PEC surface and calm sea surface
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The parabolic wave equation could predict long-range radar coverage within different environment. The wide-angle parabolic equation (WAPE) is presented in this paper, and the initial field of the parabolic equation is calculated through Green function which has a better stability and accurateness. The results of the parabolic equation (PE) have been compared with Two Ray model both above the PEC surface and the sea surface conditions, and all the results are well agreed.

articleTitle: Design of dual-band H-shaped slot antenna for 2.4 and 5 GHz wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A simple and compact dual-band H-shaped slot antenna for wireless local area network applications is proposed. The proposed antenna is composed of an H-shaped slot on the ground plane with size of 23mm by 32mm. The substrate material is foam. The antenna is fed by microstrip at its top. The impedance bandwidth, radiation pattern and gain of the antenna were simulated. The results show that the antenna just covers the WLAN bands (2.4∼2.485, 5.15∼5.35, 5.725∼5.825 GHz) with the gain remains steadily. The measurement of impedance bandwidth was carried out with a network analyzer. A good agreement between measurement and simulation can be observed.

articleTitle: Pspice/Spice simulation of MTL terminated in frequency dependent loads
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: It is difficult to analyze Multi-conductor Transmission lines (MTL) terminated in the frequency dependent loads. The impedance/admittance of the frequency dependent loads can be measured by using impedance analyzer. The frequency domain impedances/admittances are fitted by vector fitting method and a rational function is obtained. The rational function can be converted into a circuit, then Pspice/Spice model can be used to simulate this kind MTL system easily. The simulation and experimental results have been given. The results demonstrated the validity of Pspice/Spice method.

articleTitle: Local MLACA for fast solution of large-scale scattering problems based on H-matrix structure
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, the local multilevel adaptive cross approximation (LMLACA) based on multilevel partition with H-matrix structure is developed. This structure can reduce the number of leaves related to the sub-block impedance matrix. In order to reduce the CPU memory and time further, variable tolerance of ACA algorithm based on physical mechanism is adopted. It is decided according to the distance between the two interaction sub-blocks. Numerical Results demonstrate the efficiency of LMLACA.

articleTitle: Design and analysis of a novel ultra wide-band antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A new printed slot antenna is proposed, which is analyzed by the finite difference time domain method. The printed antenna is fed by microstrip line, and the effect of structural parameters on the antenna property is analyzed. The proposed antenna has a wide operating bandwidth from 2.7 to 11.4 GHz defined by |S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>|<;-7.9 dB. The simulated and measured return losses and the simulated radiation patterns are given and discussed. The antenna exhibits a stable far-field pattern within the frequency band and omnidirectional radiation characteristics in H-plane can be observed.

articleTitle: Peak-to-average power ratio reduction with improved partial transmit sequence
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The iterative partial transmit sequences (IPTS) is an efficient algorithm to reduce the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) in orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), but its linear approach is easy to be trapped in a local optimum solution, thereby, an improved IPTS (I-IPTS) algorithm is proposed. In the proposed algorithm, it breaks out of the linear search, and set the phase factor achieved by the previous iteration as the initial phase factor of the current search, thus the search is more close to the optimal phase factor after repetition. Simulation results show that I-IPTS algorithm can achieve good PAPR performance with low computational complexity, thus has high feasibility.

articleTitle: On hybrid methods for modeling complex electromagnetic problems
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper presents a review of selected hybrid numerical methods for efficient solution to complex electromagnetic problems. First, recent developments in computational electromagnetics are briefly reviewed and several remaining challenges are addressed. Second, advantages of hybrid numerical methods are highlighted and hybridization strategies are described. Recent developments in hybrid numerical methods are then introduced and numerical examples are shown to demonstrate advantages of hybrid numerical methods. Future studies of hybrid techniques are finally suggested.

articleTitle: A novel variable phase shifter based on helical slow-wave structure
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A novel variable phase shifter (VPS) based on helical slow-wave structure is presented in this paper. The VPS proposed here is used in TD-SCDMA (1.7GHz-2.17GHz) frequency band. By using the structure of helical slow-wave, physical length of the novel VPS is reduced substantially compared to the conventional phase shifter. In this paper, the new structure of VPS is calculated by High-Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS), and verified by experiment.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of ionospheric propagation based on the TSNU-PSTD
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The finite difference time domain (FDTD) method for solving ionospheric propagation will waste great time and memory. In this paper, a transformed-space non-uniform pseudo-spectral time domain (TSNU-PSTD) method in cold plasma is developed and applied to the simulation of ionospheric propagation. It is reported that this technique is as efficient as the conventional uniform pseudo-spectral time domain(PSTD) with a computational complexity of O(NIogN) since the difference is only the factor of du/dz between the conventional PSTD and the TSNU-PSTD techniques. And TSNU-PSTD can eliminate undesired Gibbs phenomena on the interface of each layer of ionosphere, which could seriously deteriorate the implementation of the PSTD.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic analysis of finite and curved frequency selective surfaces using the VSIE with MLFMA
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, the hybrid volume-surface integral-equation (VSIE) approach is proposed to analyze the transmission and reflection characteristics of finite and curved frequency-selective surfaces (FSS) structures. The surface current and electric flux density is expanded by surface RWG and volume SWG basis functions, respectively. The multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) is applied to reduce the computational complexity. Simulated results are given to demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Automated design of an ultra-wideband microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Antennas optimization design using numerical algorithm is important in modern antennas research. An automatic optimization approach of antenna design based on differential evolution strategy (DE), though externally calling the solver of electromagnetic simulation software, is developed in this paper. In order to demonstrate the effectiveness and the feasibility of this method, an ultrawideband microstrip patch antenna was designed and optimized. The simulated results show that the designed antenna is applicable in UWB system, with impedance bandwidth(S11<;-10 dB) from 3.18 GHz to 13.185 GHz and percentage bandwidth up to 62.7%. Meanwhile, Omni-directional characteristics in H-plane and high gain performance are achieved. The approach establishes a foundation for application in parallel computation technology to improve the efficiency of optimization.

articleTitle: A radar imaging algorithm based on stepped-frequency signal
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In the case of multi-objective detection, the received signals by radar are the vector superposition of each scattering point. High resolution imaging is a method to distinguish the location of multi-objective. Many algorithms are used for different wideband signal. In this paper, convolution back-projection (CBP) algorithm based on stepped-frequency signal is employed to process the echoes received by antenna and obtain a high resolution two-dimension (2-D) image. After adding a receiving antenna, the height of each scattering point is also gained. The simulation results show the effectiveness of the algorithm.

articleTitle: Higher order hierarchical method of moments for 3-D electromagnetic scattering
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A higher order method of moments (MoM) is developed for 3-D electromagnetic scattering based on hierarchical higher order basis functions in the curvilinear triangular element in this paper. An improved Duffy method is presented in the higher order moment method. Numerical experiments show that the improved Duffy method leads to a higher accuracy and faster convergence version of higher-order hierarchical MoM.

articleTitle: A half e-slot broadband multilayer patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A novel compact broadband multilayer microstrip antenna with half e-slot is presented in this paper. This patch antenna has two layers, the top layer and the middle layer. Both layers of the patch antenna were connected to the ground plane with shorting wall. In this paper, we proposed a multilayer with half e-slot technique to achieve a wide impedance broadband patch antenna with small geometric size. The VSWR, gain and radiation pattern of this antenna are simulated. The measured VSWR of it is also shown in the paper. The results are discussed in detail.

articleTitle: FDTD Analysis of the lossy MTL based on piece wise linear recursive convolution
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A novel method is proposed to analyze the multi-conductor transmission lines (MTL) with frequency dependent parameters. The frequency dependent parameters are fitted by vector fitting method and rational function can be obtained. Based on the piecewise linear recursive convolution (PLRC), the FDTD formula is deduced for MTL with frequency dependent parameters. Numerical results have been presented to demonstrate the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Effect of initial accumulated charge on electromagnetic radiation of ESD
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Electromagnetic pulse radiation generated by Electrostatic discharge (ESD) would damage even destroy the normal work of the electronic system. It was usually not considering the impact of the initial accumulated charge in previous studies of ESD electromagnetic radiation. In this paper, on the basis of taking into account the cumulative effect of the initial charge, the electromagnetic radiation of ESD has been analyzed on different distance and the threshold of "near-field" and "far-field" has been calculated on different discharge voltage. The results show that under a certain discharge voltage, the electric field generated by current and current differential item is negligible compared to the accumulation of the initial charge on the electrode, which has a great influence on the "near-field". The initial accumulated charge on the role of the electric field decline rapidly with the increase in distance between the electric field point and the discharge point. The threshold of "near-field" and far-field" increased along with the discharge voltage.

articleTitle: A millimeter wave variable polarization monopulse frontend based on microstrip array antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A millimeter-wave variable polarization monopulse frontend based on microstrip array antenna is presented in this paper. The front-end consists of four millimeter wave T/R modules and a microstrip antenna with four linear polarized subarrays. The polarization of far field electric field can be configured by amplitudes and phases of the feeds. Besides the angle error of monopulse angle estimation, the polarization information of the target can be also obtained simultaneously. Digital controlled phase shifters are used to configure the phases of feeds and to change the polarization of radiation pattern. Digital virtual polarization synthesis and digital monopulse sum-difference are realized in digital processing module.

articleTitle: Research on resistor loaded branch substructure and use it in broad-band microwave equalizer designing
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Broadband problem is always a difficult problem in microwave equalizer designing. Numerical simulations and experiments show that the branch resonator as substructure is quite suitable to broadband designing. Only one can provide 5-6 Ghz bandwidth. And for a equalizer, in order to match the given attenuation curve respectively, it's attenuation and quality factor should be adjustable besides the frequency is adjustable. To solve this problem, we choose thin-film resistor loaded resonators to construct microstrip equalizer. Good results were obtained in the experiment and simulation. Microstrip resonator is the basic substructure of microstrip equalizer, it's dimension may decide frequency change points of the equalizer. Importing a thin-film resistor into the microstrip resonator and changing the location and resistance of the resistor, we can adjust the quality factor and attenuation. The influence of the the resistor and the branch on the microstrip resonator is investigated through numerical simulations and experiments. High Frequency System Simulator (HFSS) is used to show that the microstrip resonator incorporated with the thin-film resistor loaded not only can be frequency adjustable, but also can be attenuation adjustable and quality factor adjustable. In final, a 12 GHz broadband microstrip equalizer using thin-film resistor loaded microstrip resonator is designed, fabricated and measured providing an excellent verification on it's attractive feature, matching well to the TWTA requirement.

articleTitle: A decoupled parameter estimation algorithm for coherently distributed source
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, we consider the problem of estimating the parameters - the central directions of arrival (DOA) and angular spread of distributed source by one-dimension searching algorithm. An advantage of this method is that it has decoupled the central DOA and angular spread based on the steering vector which is a Schur-Hadamard product. So the central DOA can be estimated by a proposed second-order statistics in a preliminary stage without any eigendecompostion and peak-finding searching, and then angular spread is obtained by one-dimensional searching. The proposed algorithm has improved precision, low computational cost. Simulations clearly demonstrate that the algorithm is not only effective, but also enjoys better performance.

articleTitle: A novel multi-band planar monopole antenna for mobile handsets
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A novel printed multi-band planar monopole antenna for mobile handsets is proposed and analyzed by the finite difference time domain method (FDTD). The radiating patch of the proposed antenna is designed jointly with the shape of ground plane. The proposed antenna with 36 mm in height and 50 mm in width was fabricated and tested, and its operating bandwidth defined by voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) less than 2.5 covers the global system for mobile communication (GSM, 890-960 MHz), global positioning system (GPS, 1575.42 MHz), digital communication system (DCS, 1710-1880 MHz), and personal communication system (PCS, 1850-1990 MHz). Design details and experimental results are also presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of EMI and study of testing method of magnetic field in substation
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In order to measure the surface magnetic induction intensity caused by the exciting current of substation grounding grids and testing the fault of grounding grids, the EMI characteristics are obtained by measuring and analyzing the work frequency and transient EMI in substation. Based on electromagnetic induction method, the surface magnetic induction intensity is measured by advanced electronic technology in complicated EMI environment in substation. Experiments and application show that the measuring method is feasible and practical; it can be used in engineering practice of diagnosis the fault of the grounding grids.

articleTitle: Dispersion characteristics of dielectric loaded asymmetric elliptical ridge waveguide
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A kind of asymmetric elliptical ridge waveguide is presented. Variations of the cut-off wavelength, single-mode bandwidth with the ridge dimensions and the ridge position for different values of dielectric constant are investigated in detail. The field patterns of the dominant and the first higher mode are also presented. The correctness of the numerical results is verified. The results provide an extension to the existing design data for ridge waveguide and considered helpful in practical applications.

articleTitle: Novel cross-coupled filters using metamaterial split ring resonators
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, a novel metamaterial (MTM) split ring resonators for microwave bandpass filter is proposed. The effective permittivity and permeability of the filter are extracted. The extracted results show that the effective permittivity and permeability are both positive at the first half of passband and they are negative at the other part. The double positive or double negative characteristic enables the transmission of electromagnetic wave in-band while the single negative characteristic disables the transmission out-of-band. The theory of metamaterial and the NRW (Nicolson-Ross-Weir) approach to verify its double negative characteristics are briefly introduced. From the simulation results one can see that the filter has advantages of small dimension, low in-band insertion loss and good out-of-band suppressed and linearity.

articleTitle: Efficient PML implementation for truncating nonlinear FDTD lattices based on the Z-transform method
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A simple and efficient implementation of the stretched coordinate perfectly matched layer (SC-PML) based on the Z-transform method is proposed for truncating one-dimensional nonlinear dispersive finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) lattices. The main advantage of the proposed PML formulations is that no auxiliary variable is required to update the electric flux density and the magnetic field in one-dimensional case. The proposed algorithm is validated through a numerical example carried out in one-dimensional domain which includes Lorentz dispersion as well as Kerr and Raman nonlinearities.

articleTitle: Parallel FDTD analysis of large-scale ridged TEM horn antenna array
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Parallel computation is an effective way to solve large-scale electromagnetic problems which can provide enough computer memory and reduce the computing time. In this paper the program of the parallel Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) based on the JASMIN framework is proposed. The parallel FDTD program was used for simulating the electric dipole source and a ridged TEM horn antenna. The obtained parallel efficiency was as high as 80% even when 128 computers were employed. Numerical results show that the program is correct and efficient. A large-scale array of ridged TEM horn antenna was simulated. Its near-field and far-field results were given. The example provides a solution for studying large-scale antenna array and shows that the program has the ability to solve large-scale electromagnetic problems.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of bulk left-handed metamaterials composed of coplanar magnetic and electric resonators
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A bulk left-handed metamaterial (LHM) composed of coplanar magnetic and electric resonators was fabricated and investigated experimentally. The measurement results show a 0.5 GHz wide left-handed band, which verifies the validity of the bulk LHM.

articleTitle: Ka-band spatial power dividing/combing transition circuit
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A Ka-Band spatial power dividing/combing hybrid transition circuit using rectangular waveguide connector is presented. The simulation model of this power divider/combiner structure is developed. A four-way waveguide power dividing/combing circuit has been designed, fabricated and tested. In the frequency range of 34 to 36 GHz, the return loss is less than 15 dB, and the insert loss is better than 1.8 dB, which indicate that this power dividing/combing hybrid transition circuit has the advantages of low insertion loss and compact size. Good agreement is obtained between the measured results and the simulated results.

articleTitle: Implementation and performance comparison for higher order triangular vector elements
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Based on H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>(curl) triangular interpolatory vector elements, explicit forms of the elemental matrices for the higher order vector elements are presented completely by using the classified bases and block matrix technique, the explicit results of integration matrices are also given. The results of a numerical experiment that investigates the eigen-problem of a rectangular waveguide, compare the performance of different vector elements systematically (such as calculated accuracy, condition numbers, selectivity of the facet related basis functions), which are also applied to the eigen-solution of homogeneously-filled waveguides. The methods can be extended to the analysis of 3D, ultra higher order, hierarchical vector elements with any type effectively.

articleTitle: Unconditionally stable PSTD method based on weighted Laguerre polynomial expansion
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A novel unconditionally stable (US) pseudo-spectral time-domain (PSTD) method is implemented by virtue of weighted Laguerre polynomial expansion. This novel algorithm preserves both unconditional stability and less spatial resolution and hence is proved to be an efficient and accurate method. Numerical examples are included to verify the validity of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Analysis of doublet antenna with finite frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, a rigorous method based on the surface integral equation is applied to analyze a doublet antenna with finite FSS radome. The surface integral equation is solved using the method of moments (MOM). The method is then used to study the effects of the finite FSS on the radiation characteristics of antenna system.

articleTitle: Optimization of broadband circularly polarized wide-slot antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, a new circularly-polarized antenna consisting of a circular wide-slot loaded by three radial metal strips is designed. By adjusting the proper position and length of each strip using optimization procedure of constrained multi-objective genetic algorithm combined with simulation software, the axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of the antenna along the normal vector is broadened, and the 13.9% common bandwidth for 1 dB AR and -10 dB return loss (RL) is achieved. Furthermore, the AR deteriorated with angle at different frequencies are displayed and studied.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic engineering simulation techniques using parallel EM simulation tools
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, we present some basic ideas to use EM software package to accurately simulate the EM problems. The basic procedure in the EM simulation includes excitation setting, mesh design, boundary setting and parallel processing design for a parallel code. In the paper, we introduce some simulation techniques using different software packages and use these software packages to simulate some typical examples.

articleTitle: Analysis on TM0 mode's resonant characteristic of cylindrical resonator loaded with complicated dielectric
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Microwave cavity with complicated structure dielectric and hollow center is investigated by mode matching method. By deducing eigen equation and calculating resonant frequencies of TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> mode, main factors that influence resonant frequencies is studied. In addition, the resonant frequencies of TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> mode is compared with commercial software (CST) results. The results show good agreement between computations and CST simulations. It can be seen that this method is of high credibility and efficiency. This paper is of great significance for cavity design and theoretical perfection.

Author Keywords: cylindrical resonator loaded with complicated dielectric

articleTitle: Ship detection with adaptive parameter based on detection background analysis
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Contaminated with various clutter, such as sea clutter, ionospheric interference, earth echoes, in HF surface wave radar (HFSWR), detection background seldom follows a uniform probability distribution. The ideal suppositions by the classical detection algorithms limit the detection performance of the operational system. Thus this paper proposes a new detection architecture which can classify and identify the detection background in real time to improve the detection performance. Firstly, the detection background is classified into five parts with a criterion based on the results of background region segmentation. Then, using the statistical analysis of the classified detection background, a detection method with adaptive parameters is proposed which can select the proper background distribution parameters based on the type of the reference cells. Finally, real data are used for verifying the advantages of the proposed method comparing with three detection algorithms for HF radar introduced in literature recently.

articleTitle: Amplitude characteristics of microwave induced thermoacoustic signals
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: When pulsed radio-frequency (RF) or pulsed microwave irradiation is absorbed by biological tissue, the expansion of the heated tissue, derived from the absorption of electromagnetic energy, leads to an instantaneous acoustic stress or pressure distribution inside the tissue, which prompting wave propagation toward the surface of the tissue. In this paper, we present a theoretical analysis of the amplitude characteristics of microwave induced thermoacoustic (MITA) signals based on the thermal equation and dynamical equation. Then a brief introduction to the prototype of MITA tomography experimental system is given. And two groups of experiment have been carried out. The experimental results are used to validate the theoretical analysis and also may be employed to evaluate the limitation of microwave power for safety reasons as well as the availability of signals for reconstruction.

articleTitle: Transmission characteristics of dielectric loaded asymmetric V ridge waveguide
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A kind of asymmetric V ridge waveguide is presented. Variations of the cut-off wavelength, single-mode bandwidth with the ridge dimensions and the ridge position for different values of dielectric constant are investigated in detail. The field patterns of the dominant are presented. The correctness of the numerical results is verified. The results provide an extension to the existing design data for ridge waveguide and considered helpful in practical applications.

articleTitle: An improved COST - WI model in metropolitan Areas
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: An extension model is proposed by combination the statistical method with COST 231-Walfisch-Ikegami radio model. It is assumed that the building height is not deterministic variable like those in theory propagation models, but a statistical variable. The performance of the model is studied by simulating probability density functions (PDF), cumulative distribution functions (CDF), level cross rate (LCR) and average fade duration (AFD). Finally, we emphasize the proposed model by the marginal communication probability and the rate of the valid service area.

articleTitle: A novel miniaturized microstrip spiral antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Microstrip antennas have many applications in various communicational systems. To meet the requirement of miniaturization of the carry-home equipments, a novel spiral microstrip antenna is, described. The new design is made on conventional microstrip spiral antenna, and the dimension of the antenna is reduced nearly 40% compared with the conventional spiral antenna. Furthermore, the new designed antenna has a bidirectional radiation pattern because of the small ground plate below the bottom of the substrate.The configuration of the antenna is simple and easy to fabricate. Details of the proposed antenna design and simulation results were presented and discussed. The simulation results show the validity of the design.

articleTitle: Preconditioned adaptive integral method for the analysis of planar microstrip structures
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Adaptive integral method based on far-field expansion is introduced to speed up the analysis of the planar microstrip structure. The auxiliary basis functions are constructed as superposition of point-like current elements located on rectangular grids which reproduce the same far field as generated from the original basis functions.
