Then it is able to employ the fast Fourier transform technique to speed up the matrix vector multiplication required by the iterative solver. The resultant linear systems are then preconditioned by the symmetric successive over relaxation technique to further accelerate iteration. Compared to the previous scheme, the proposed algorithm makes a reduction in both the computational complexity and the storage requirement to attain the same precision.

articleTitle: Development and testing of a 3.9GHz power coupler for a superconducting particle accelerator cavity
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Superconducting cavities offer the advantage of high field intensity for a given input power, making them an attractive contender for particle accelerator applications [1]. Power coupling into a superconducting cavity employed in a particle accelerator requires unique provisions to maintain high vacuum and cryogenic temperature on the cavity side, while operating with ambient conditions on the source side. Components introduced to fulfill mechanical requirements must show negligible obstruction of the propagation of the microwave with absence of critical locations that may give rise to electron multipaction and thermal breakdown, leading to a multiple section design, instead of an aperture, a probe, or a loop structure as found in conventional cavities. A coaxial power coupler for a superconducting multiple-cell cavity at 3.9 GHz has been developed at Fermilab. The cavity is intended to be employed as an accelerator to provide enhanced electron beam quality for a free-electron laser in the Hamburg user facility.

articleTitle: Scattering computation of slightly rough Gaussian surfaces by Kirchhoff approach with harmonic extraction analysis
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic wave scattering from rough surfaces has been the subject of intensive investigations over the past several decades for its applications in a number of important remote sensing implementations. For slightly rough surfaces that the radius of curvature of surface is bigger than the wavelength, the Kirchhoff method is the most commonly used approach. In this paper a new way for scattering computation from rough surfaces is introduced. Here Kirchhoff approach is applied for considering the electromagnetic wave interaction with slightly rough Gaussian surfaces. Fourier series of rough Gaussian surface is used for extracting the strong harmonics of the surface. Then by using the Kirchhoff formulation for periodic surfaces, scattering coefficient is computed. It is shown that by strong harmonics extraction of the rough surface, the acceptable results could be attained. This method could be useful in ray tracing. Asphalt surfaces are simulated by this method in millimeter-wave band. The results are also validated with the method of moments.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized high-gain printed antennas for small satellite applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Two new circularly polarized printed antennas are designed and simulated. The characteristics of the antennas are obtained in terms of return loss, gain, bandwidth and axial ratio. Some simulated results are discussed. To broaden the impedance bandwidth, an air gap configuration is utilized. To broaden the axial ratio bandwidth, a dual feed is adopted. To increase the gain of the circularly polarized antenna, a parasitic patch above the driven patch is used as a director. To reduce the dimensions and broaden the 3-dB axial ratio beamwidth, a rim is introduced. Detailed parameters and simulated results of the proposed antennas are given. The circularly polarized high-gain antennas can be used in satellite data down links thanks to its advantages of low cost and easy fabrication. Simulation of the proposed antenna mounted on a typical micro satellite at Surrey has been done and some results are given which demonstrates the reliable performance.

articleTitle: Time domain behaviours of a small quasi-self-complementary UWB antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, a time domain study of a small quasi-self-complementary UWB antenna is presented. First, a brief description of antenna configuration and its frequency domain behaviours are illustrated. Thereafter, a comprehensive time domain investigation of the antenna is highlighted. It has been shown that the small quasi-self-complementary UWB antenna generally demonstrates a good performance in both the frequency and the time domain.

articleTitle: Compact multilayer coupled stripline LTCC filter with defected ground structure
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A novel multilayer coupled stripline resonator structure is introduced to realize miniature broadband band-pass filter using low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) process with defected ground structure (DGS). Wide bandwidth and good selectivity are obtained by exploiting four resonators and the filter exhibits a high rejection in stopband by adopting the tapered DGS. Moreover, an inductance feed back between the output and input is introduced to produce transmission zeros. Filter with size of λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> /12 × λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> /12 × h (λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the wavelength at the midband frequency; h is the substrate height) is designed, fabricated and measured. The measured responses agree well with simulation results.

articleTitle: Bandwidth characteristic of arbitrarily trapezoidal groove waveguide with method of moment
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Using method of moment, the single mode bandwidth properties of arbitrarily trapezoidal groove waveguide is obtained and discussed. There is a minimum of bandwidth along with inclination angle. It is of important values in theoretical studies and practical engineering applications of arbitrarily trapezoidal groove guide for millimeter waves.

articleTitle: An embedded LTCC stripline bandpass filter for millimeter-wave system on package
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper presents a low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) bandpass filter, which is embedded into an eleven-layer substrate. A quasi-coaxial structure is employed to reduce the impedance discontinuity caused by GCPW to stripline transition. Vertical metal vias are utilized to realize grounding and shielding for the stripline filter. The measurements of the fabricated filter show an insertion loss of 4.5 dB and a 1.73 GHz passband with the centre frequency at 34.69 GHz, including the two RF coaxial connectors. The measured return loss in the passband is lower than -13.45 dB. The whole bandpass filter occupies an area of 9.8 mm × 5 mm × 1.1 mm. The compact configuration and measured performance show that the filter is suit for millimeter-wave system on package.

articleTitle: Research on MMW variable polarization monopulse microstrip array antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In order to realize the compact monopulse variable polarization antenna, the development of a Ka-band monopulse variable polarization antenna is presented, based on polarization synthesis theory. The loss of the feed network is reduced by using space power combing technique. This kind of microstrip array antenna consists of several linearly polarized subarrays of rotational symmetry, and change the polarization mode by adjusting the amplitude and phase of each subarray. The simulation of the four subarrays shows that this antenna using sequential rotation method has great advantages, such as simple, high polarization purity, low loss and so on. Analysis of the effects of the antenna beam caused by amplitude and phase inconsistency of each subarray is carried on, and the actual requirement of amplitude and phase consistency is put forward.

articleTitle: The primary study on the theory and application of time-reversal focusing with electromagnetic wave
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, the theory of time-reversal focusing with electromagnetic wave is investigated. The finite difference time domain (FDTD) method is applied to simulate the time-reversal(TR) process. In the process, the propagation of time-reversal electromagnetic wave in homogeneous and inhomogeneous medium is discussed respectively. In both cases, the electromagnetic wave diverging from a point source propagates and is received by two antennas set on each side of the medium. The received signals are time reversed and retransmitted back by the corresponding antennas in their original paths. The resulting waves converge back to point of its initial source. The numerical simulation verifies the ability of time-reversal spatial-temporal focusing in electromagnetism.

articleTitle: Interferometric ISAR imaging for RCS and three-dimensional target characteristics measurements
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Target characteristics are measured using variable methods, interferometric ISAR technology is used to get three dimension signature and RCS from a target. The model of interferometric ISAR is set up, the structure of the system with a single transmitter and two receivers is designed. Then eight scatterers model is supposed, two ISAR images can be got at the same time after the back projection reconstruction algorithm, and the inteferometric image can be got. Numerical simulation verifies that this method is available.

articleTitle: Novel weakly conditionally stable FDTD scheme based on trapezoidal recursive convolution for modeling dispersive media
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The letter presents a novel weakly conditionally stable finite-difference time-domain (WCS-FDTD) method using the trapezodial recursive convolution (TRC) technique for modeling dispersive media. The new scheme not only allows much larger time step compared with traditional FDTD , but also maintain the accuracy comparable to the piecewise linear RC (PLRC) technique The implementation of the new scheme is also simpler than its PLRC-WCS-FDTD counterpart.

articleTitle: A circuit-oriented model for gapped power-ground planes
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In gapped power-ground planes, there is strong coupling between two sides of narrow slot. So the modeling of the gapped PG planes needs to take into account this coupling. In this paper, a circuit-oriented model is proposed for analyzing the characteristics of PG planes. An integral equation equivalent circuit (IEEC) method is used to model the arbitrary shaped PG pair, and transmission lines method is used to model the coupling of the slot. The two circuit models are combined in SPICE-like simulator, then the whole model of the gapped power-ground planes is formulated. The circuit-oriented model has been validated by commercial software HFSS. The proposed method can be used to predict the effect of decoupling capacitances.

articleTitle: Calibration switch of the spaceborne microwave radiometer
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: When the spaceborne microwave radiometer operates in orbit, the microwave switch allows for three different input sources: the observation antenna, the calibration antenna, and the matched load at ambient temperature. When one port of the switch is connected, the sources from the other two unconnected ports will leaks into the connected port if their isolations are not great enough. In this paper, the contributions from the unconnected ports to the connected port are analyzed and how to choose the isolation of the switch is considered.

articleTitle: A method of angle error extraction for monopulse radar with 3-subarray variable polarization antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: To improve the ability of radar's anti-jamming and target recognition, polarization technology is applied to monopulse angle measurement. 3-subarray millimetre wave variable polarization array antenna is also proposed and discussed in this paper. A novel method of angle error extraction in horizontal and vertical direction is given by analyzing polarization synthesis and electric field of the antenna, meanwhile, the difference between the new method and traditional one is discussed. Finally, according to the new method, simulation results of angle error extraction are presented.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo method for Dirichlet boundary condition of multi-media field
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: At present Monte Carlo method is widely used in nuclear science, statistical physics, medicine, materials science, economics and other disciplines, However, it is lagging behind in calculating of the electromagnetic field, especially for multi-media field. There are two kinds of Monte Carlo methods, one is fixed random walk, the other is floating random walk. This paper mainly introduces the application of the two kinds of Monte Carlo method for multi-media field two-dimensional Dirichlet boundary condition, and compare to the two kinds of methods by an example.

articleTitle: Factorized sparse approximate inverse preconditioning strategies for MLFMA
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: We consider the solution of large electromagnetic scattering problems involving three-dimensional arbitrarily shaped targets using the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). One kind of parallel sparse approximation inverse preconditioner is employed to reduce the iteration counts for the solutions of the electric-field integral equation (EFIE) and the combined-field integral equation (CFIE). Even though CFIE produces better conditioned systems compared to EFIE, we still need EFIE for problems involving open geometries since CFIE is limited to the solution of closed geometries.

articleTitle: Investigation of crosstalk between wires using PEEC
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The existence of parasitical parameters, such as coupling inductances and coupling capacitance between wires, makes crosstalk inevitable. In order to investigate the effect of crosstalk, accurately and efficiently computing of parasitical parameters is needed. In this paper, Partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) method is used to partition the model of wires and ground plane, to extract the partial parameters of resistances, capacitances and inductances forming the equivalent SPICE circuit and to analyze the effect of crosstalk. Different kinds of relative position of wires are considered.

articleTitle: A design methodology for efficiency improvement of CMOS class-E power amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis on efficiency improvement of class-E power amplifiers (PAs) with Microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) inductors. The efficiency can be improved and has been demonstrated by using MEMS inductors. The proposed MEMS technology is validated by a prototype MEMS inductor. Also, the simulation result of MEMS inductors by HFSS have good match with the measured result. The stacked-metal layer inductors implemented in MEMS process are developed for increasing the quality factor. The simulation result of a CMOS class-E PA with MEMS inductors shows that the increased quality factor of inductors by 2 can improve the drain efficiency by 6%. Therefore, we present a design methodology that can improve the efficiency of PAs by optimizing the quality factor of fully integrated inductors.

articleTitle: Effect of Ge composition on the ballasting resistor of RF power SiGe HBTs
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A new expression for the thermal stability factor S of power HBTs is presented in this paper, considering the temperature dependence of collector saturation current. Based on the expression, the accurate minimum emitter ballasting resistance (<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">REmin</sub>) of the HBTs that is necessary in the thermal stability condition is determined. It is found that for SiGe HBTs, the R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Emin</sub> decreases with the increasing operating temperature in the high temperature region due to the existence of Ge composition in SiGe base whereas for Si BJTs, the R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Emin</sub> increases monotonously with the operation temperature. Hence for high-temperature-operation SiGe HBTs, the additional emitter ballasting resistance can be decrease so as to minimize adverse effect of the ballasting resistance as possible. These results provide a good guide to design emitter ballasting resistance of power HBTs and high-temperature-operation HBTs.

articleTitle: Wideband Electromagnetic coupled ellipse LTCC antenna for Ka band
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper presents a planar antenna in low-temperature co-fired ceramic technology for a sing-package. The antenna has an elliptical radiator fed through a coplanar waveguide transmission line, and four slots are etched on the elliptical patch to adjust the path and length of the current, improving the return loss characteristics (especially in low frequency) and bandwidth performance. The proposed antenna has been simulated and analyzed. Results show that the prototype antenna has achieved a bandwidth of 30 GHz, from 25 GHz to 55 GHz. Additionally, the effects of varying parameter values of the structure have been investigated. The LTCC antenna occupies only 4 × 4 × 0.576 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: 3D simulation of reverberation chamber by using parallel computing clusters
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: We select reverberation chamber for this study, with using method of FDTD, combining with parallel computing to simulate the interior distribution. From the simulation results, we analyzed the mesh generation of parallel treatment and the calculation efficiency.

articleTitle: An improved equivalent circuit parameters extraction method for dumbbell-shape DGS
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The paper presents an improved equivalent circuit parameters extraction method for the dumbbell-shape defect ground structure (DGS). The DGS unit with center frequency of 5 GHz were designed and fabricated on a TLX substrate with thickness of 1 mm and dielectric constant of 2.55. The equivalent circuit simulated results are in good agreement with the measured results. It can be widely used for the design and analysis of DGS .

articleTitle: Analysis of microstrip discontinuities and their compensation via the finite difference time domain method
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The characteristics of the typical microstrip discontinuities, such as right-angle bends, T junctions and steps in width, are investigated based on the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method in a wide-frequency range. The compensation methods of the microstrip discontinuities are also discussed and compensated discontinuities can improve the circuit performance as well as the bandwidth compared with the uncompensated. The electric field varying with signal traveling in the spatial and time domain at the microstrip discontinuities are also presented.

articleTitle: MPI-based parallel FDTD investigation on the electromagnetic scattering from the two-layered rough surface with a large angle incidence
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: MPI-based parallel FDTD algorithm for the electromagnetic scattering from two-layered randomly rough surfaces is presented in the paper. And the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) medium is adopted for truncation of FDTD lattices, in which the finite-difference equations can be used for the total computation domain by properly choosing the uniaxial parameters. This makes the parallel FDTD algorithm easier to implement. The parallel performance with different processes is illustrated for one rough surface realization, and the computation time of parallel FDTD algorithm is dramatically reduced compared to a single-process implementation.

articleTitle: Influence of HIGP on ground-reliance to monopole antennas
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The adjustment of antennas on high speed train is a troublesome problem in engineering. In this paper, the influence of ground-plane to monopole antennas is studied. Then the high impendence ground-plane (HIGP) structure is introduced and applied to the antenna. The results of such antenna with and without the HIGP structure are compared. Simulation and experiment results show that HIGP structure can reduce the ground-reliance of the monopole antennas.

articleTitle: GSM/DCS dual-band bandpass filter design using hybrid parameter elements
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This paper presents a design of GSM/DCS dual-band filter based on hybrid parameter elements. General microwave dual-band bandpass filter is realized by using lumped parameter elements only. Using two different parameters elements can combine advantages of two different parameters elements to meet engineering application requirement. Actual measured results of the filter sample are in good agreement with simulated results.

articleTitle: Integrated LTCC transmitter module at Ku band
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A Ku-band transmitter module which is fully integrated in low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) environment is presented in the paper. The module consists of two T/R switches, one phase shifter, one attenuator, one power amplifier and a circulator. Each of them is designed and assembled individually using Ferro's A6M tapes for the feasibility of the transmitter module. The switch shows a maximum in-band insertion loss of -1.84 dB. The power amplifier shows a measured gain of 30.4 dB and a 1 dB compression output power of 28.2 dBm at 16 GHz. The microstrip circulator exhibits a maximum insertion loss of -0.84 dB at 15.52 GHz. The measured module gives a total gain of 15.4 dB and a ldB compression output power of 22.1 dBm at 16 GHz. This transmitter module has a compact size of 24 × 22 × 1.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>.

articleTitle: Parallelization of multilevel fast multipole algorithm with open MPI for scattering by large scale targets
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, we present the parallelization of multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) for three-dimensional scattering problems of large scale objects. A new, full MPI-2 supported implementation, named Open MPI, is adopted in our code as the parallel communication library. We compare the performance of the parallel code based on Open MPI and MPICH, the numerical result shows that Open MPI performs better than MPICH as a parallel library for our code. Besides, a novel method is proposed for reducing the truncation number without any loss of accuracy. The capability and accuracy of the parallel code are demonstrated by considering a sphere of 150λ discretized with 20,919,633 unknowns and a square patch of 200λ discretized with 10,150,143 unknowns.

articleTitle: The SSOR preconditioned bi-conjugate gradient iterative solver for finite element solution of scattering problems
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, the finite element method (FEM) is used for the simulation of scattering problems. The SSOR-BCG solver is used for the solution of the FEM linear system. The accuracy of FEM and the efficiency of SSOR-BiCG are tested by simulating the scattering of a lossy dielectric sphere in the final of the paper.

articleTitle: MOM analysis of the planar and curved FSS based on dipole elements
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A method of moments (MOM) technique using the EFIE is described for the simulation of finitely dipole array FSS, involving both planar and cylindrically curved structures. An equivalent strip model for the wire structure is used, and RWG basis function is adopted in MOM analysis. Some characteristics of the curved FSS are studied, and the effect of mutual coupling between the FSS radome and the antenna is discussed.

articleTitle: A novel slow-wave ladder dual-mode bandpass filter
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A novel type of slow-wave dual-mode bandpass filter with periodic ladder microstrip lines is presented. This filter has better stopband rejection and wider stopband, in comparison with the conventional square ring dual-mode bandpass filter. It is designed at the operating frequency of 6 GHz with the bandwidth of 500 MHz. Size reduction has been achieved by means of the slow-wave structure. A dual-mode bandpass filter using this structure was fabricated and measured, and the measured results agree well with those of simulation.

articleTitle: Exact modeling and computation using MLFMA of an antenna array with a radome structure
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The exact model of an antenna array with a dielectric radome is established by using the surface integral equations (SIE) and method of moments (MoM). The multilevel fast multipole algorithm(MLFMA) is used to reduce the memory occupation and accelerate the iteration convergence of the conjugate gradient (CG) method. Based on the validation of the correctness of the algorithm, some electrically large antenna-radome system are numerically simulated, and their radiation characteristics are analyzed.

articleTitle: An ultra-wideband planar monopole antenna with band-notched characteristics
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A square metal-plate monopole UWB antenna with band-notched property is proposed. The antenna consists of a square metal plate with two bevel-cuts, an inverted V-shaped slot, and a perfect ground plane, and exhibits low return loss property (|S11|<;-10 dB) within most of the UWB band. A band notched characteristic within 5-6 GHz is noted, this property can be used to avoid EM interference between UWB system and existing wireless systems. The antenna is analyzed by FDTD method, and the results are essentially in agreement with those of experiment. The results show that the antenna can be applied to the UWB systems for its ultrawideband property and simple structure.

articleTitle: New directions in computational electromagnetics
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Computational EM (CEM) is a very active field, as is evident from a quick glance at the literature, comprising of journal papers as well as proceedings of symposia in the areas of Antennas, Propagation, Microwave Circuits, and Metamaterials, just to name a few. A variety of CEM tools that are based on the Integral Equation techniques, e.g., the MoM and TDIE, and Finite Methods such as the FEM and FDTD, are available to us for solving a wide range of EM problems. The above CEM methods have recently been embellished by combining them with innovative techniques such as the FMM for MoM-based algorithms, Discontinuous Galerkin approach for FEM, and extensive Parallelization for the FDTD. This development has, in turn, enlarged the scope of the type and size of currently solvable problems that would have been totally unthinkable even just 10 years ago. So, we can rest assured that CEM is not a dead field after all, as some self-appointed pundits would have us believe.

articleTitle: Bandwidth characteristic of arbitrarily V-shaped groove waveguide with method of moment
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The V-shaped groove guide with arbitrary inclination angle has been studied with method of moment. The single mode bandwidth properties has been obtained and discussed. It is of important values in theoretical studies and practical engineering applications of arbitrarily V-shaped groove guide for millimeter waves.

articleTitle: A microwave sensor design for on-line moisture determination of turbine oil
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: It is important to monitor the moisture content of the oil during the operation of turbine. Such applications require the sensor can provide relative long time, continuous, and accurate measurements. In this paper, a new integrated on-line microwave moisture sensor system is presented. The moisture sensor is based on the principle that the permittivity of the two materials mixture can be calculated by measuring the resonant frequency. The relationship between the moisture content and resonant frequency is obtained by using of the perturbation theory analysis and dielectric mixture theory. Detailed sensor design is on the basis of the consideration of sensitivity, dynamic range, liquidity, coupling and temperature calibration. The measure system is implemented with circulator, PLL, detector, temperature sensor, signal processing part and LCD display. Temperature calibration in the practical application is also included.

articleTitle: A CPW fed antenna with ring strip ground for ultra-wideband applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: A new structure of ultra-wideband antenna is proposed. The antenna consists of a ring strip connecting with two triangle patches as the ground, and a rectangular patch connecting with a strip as the radiator and feeding line. The antenna is fed by a coplanar waveguide. Simulated results gotten by FDTD method are given and compared with the experimental results. The results show that the antenna can cover a bandwidth from 2.8 to 11 GHz for return loss less than -10 dB.

articleTitle: Design and manufacture of the wide-band probe-feed stacked microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: The C-band wide band probe-feed stacked microstrip antenna is studied and manufactured. Based on the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method, a parametric study of the input impedance of the antenna is presented, and the effects of some parameters are illustrated. The structure of screw-bracket-support is used for the manufacture of this kind of antenna to achieve the thickness adjustable air layer. And several notes for manufacture are considered based on the parameter analysis. The measured input impedance bandwidth (VSWR ≤ 2) and the 1 dB gain bandwidth are more than 20%. The measured results are basically accordant to numerical simulated results, so it testified the capability of the model in expanding bandwidth and validity of this structure. The radiation patterns within operation bandwidth are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: A deceptive jamming method against MMW monopulse radar
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: This article focuses on MMW monopulse radar seeker and its deceptive jamming technique. Based on the principle of stepped-frequency high range profile monopulse seeker, a method of jamming against stepped-frequency high range profile monopulse seeker is proposed. The theory of stepped-frequency high range profile monopulse seeker is given in detail. The system architecture, theory foundation and principles of the jamming against stepped-frequency high range profile monopulse seeker are described in detail in this paper. The method shows that the high range profile of the monopulse seeker could be deceived successfully based on the pulling-off of the range track gate with false high range profile. Lastly, the conclusions and future works are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Immune genetic algorithm-based parameters optimization of cognitive radios
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: Genetic algorithms are best suited for optimization problems. But premature convergence exists when genetic algorithm applied for optimization problems. The immune genetic algorithm (IGA) combined artificial immune system and GA together is presented to overcome this problem. Finally, the IGA is used to solve parameter optimization problems of cognitive radios. Simulation results demonstrate that IGA can rapidly reach an optimal decision.

articleTitle: Study on resonant characteristic of microwave cavity loaded with complex structure dielectric in rubidium frequency standard
publicationTitle: 2009 International Conference on Microwave Technology and Computational Electromagnetics (ICMTCE 2009)
abstract: In this paper, the mode matching method is used to analyze resonant characteristic of microwave resonant cavity loaded with complex structure dielectric in rubidium atomic frequency standard. By calculating the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode's resonant frequency and comparing with theoretical and simulation software (CST) results, the correctness of this method has been proved. Numerical results show that the resonant frequency is related to the length, thickness of the cavity cell as well as the loaded dielectric of the cavity. The obtained outcomes give a certain theoretical value on the theoretical perfection of resonant cavity loaded with dielectric and the design of resonant cavity in atomic frequency standard.
